about: The priest asks the Holy Trinity to receive the offering made in memory of Christ's passion, resurrection and ascension, and in honour of the Blessed Virgin Mary and the saints. In the final petition, their intercession in heaven corresponds to the keeping of their memory on earth.

s01.narrative: The priest returns to the middle of the altar, bows slightly, and with joined hands resting on it offers the whole sacrifice together.

s02.translation: Receive, holy Trinity, this offering, which we offer Thee in memory of the passion, the resurrection and the ascension of Jesus Christ our Lord: and in honour of blessed Mary ever Virgin, and of blessed John the Baptist, and of the holy Apostles Peter and Paul, and of these, and of all the Saints: that it may profit them unto honour and us unto salvation: and may they deign to intercede for us in heaven, whose memory we keep on earth. Through the same Christ our Lord. Amen.

w001.function: The same word that began the prayer over the host. The last of the offering prayers takes up what the first opened with.

w003.function: The vocative is the same as the nominative. The address settles it.

w005.function: The noun of offérre — the thing brought before God.

w010.function: Ob, always with the accusative, means “on account of”. The same memory returns at the prayer's end as “memóriam” (w059).

w014.function: The third of three genitives depending on “memóriam” (w010): the Passion, Resurrection and Ascension.

w021.function: The change of preposition marks a change of ground: memory of Christ, honour of the saints.

w035.function: Almost the Confíteor’s list of saints, here in the genitive — without Michael the Archangel, and with “istórum” (w037) added.

w037.function: The demonstrative of what is close at hand: the saints whose relics are in this altar.

w042.function: Dative of advantage: it is to be of honour to them.

w049.function: Two sides of one offering: honour to them, salvation to us.

w051.function: Nominative plural, the subject of “dignéntur” (w055). The same form also serves the dative singular.

w054.function: The infinitive completing “dignéntur” (w055): what the saints are asked to deign to do — step in with God on our behalf.

w062.function: “in cælis” and “in terris” each close their own clause: they there, we here.

w064.function: Idem is is with the ending -dem, “the same one”. Before d the m turns to n — hence eúndem, not eúmdem.
